Far more prominent is Naaman the Syrian, commander of Aram's army, whose healing from leprosy through Elisha's instruction to wash in the Jordan became one of Scripture's most celebrated narratives of faith beyond Israel's borders (2 Kgs 5:1–27). Jesus himself cited Naaman's healing as evidence that God's mercy extends to outsiders (Luke 4:27)."
